correctness.rationale: The indicators all have squared norm r; each is a vertex (a 0/1 vector cannot be a nontrivial convex combination of different 0/1 vectors). For the minimum-norm point c of their hull, ⟨c,v−c⟩≥0 for every vertex v. Any convex representation of c therefore has positive coefficients only on vertices with equality. Those are precisely the contacts at squared distance r−||c||²; their weighted squared distances to any candidate y average to r−||c||²+||y−c||², proving unique optimality. For handle mass h the within-block means minimize the squared norm and attain (r−h)²/p+h²/t; they are in the hull for every 0≤h≤1 by interpolation between the two orbit barycenters. This strictly convex quadratic has unconstrained minimum at rt/(p+t), so h=min(rt/(p+t),1). This gives both stated centers, the two radii, and the squared-radius deficit by completing the square. In the capped regime, the inner products of the two types differ by (r−1)/p−1/t, giving the exact positive squared-distance clearance. At equality c is uniform and both orbits contact, including the orbit not needed to support c. Orbit sizes and parameter scope are correct. The supplement contains four off-center probes and one centered probe, rather than five off-center probes as described; this has no bearing on the analytic theorem. The supplement was inspected read-only.
residual_risks: The statement uses the canonical Euclidean indicator realization; it is not an affine-invariant result.

evidence: For h=Σ_B x_i, Cauchy–Schwarz in the blocks reduces the prior dual to minimizing (r−h)²/p+h²/t over 0≤h≤1. Equality is attained at the componentwise block means. The optimizer is min(rt/(p+t),1), and the radius deficit is ((r−1)t−p)_+²/(pt(p+t)) by completing the square.

Below or at the switch the block means agree, so all vertices contact. Above it the pure-pan inner product exceeds the handle-orbit inner product by (r−1)/p−1/t; this gives the asserted departing orbit and its exact clearance. The p=r catalogue formula has cutoff rt=r+t and supercritical squared radius 2−(r+t)/(rt), both agreeing with the specialization, but alone it does not imply p>r.

value.rationale: The canonical Euclidean invariant is a legitimate question, and the contact pattern is stated accurately, but its computation is a routine equal-norm-ball conversion and a one-constraint scalar projection. The sharp threshold, departures, and deficit are direct consequences of the already available geometry and constraints; the frozen record adds no independent obstruction, mechanism, or unknown exact invariant beyond that calculation.
residual_risks: The formula can still be useful as a worked example or reference value; that is distinct from meeting the bar for a new finding.
